name: Docling
short: Turns PDFs into clean text and tables, on your own laptop.
plain: IBM's open-source converter that reads PDFs the way you see them, so tables, headings and code blocks come out cleanly for your RAG app.
use_when: Your documents are mostly text and simple tables, and you don't want to send files to the cloud.
skip_when: Your papers are full of maths formulas or complex tables. Try MinerU instead.
note: Needs PyTorch, which is a big download. It eats your RAM, not an API bill.

name: MinerU
short: Reads complex PDFs, turns formulas into LaTeX.
plain: A document parser that uses a vision model to understand layouts, converting equations to LaTeX and complex tables to Markdown.
use_when: You work with STEM, economics or medical papers full of formulas and dense tables.
skip_when: You need to process lots of simple documents fast.
note: For college papers with maths, accuracy matters more than speed. Worth testing side by side with Docling.

name: RAGatouille
short: ColBERT retrieval in a few lines of Python.
plain: Makes ColBERT, a very precise search model that keeps every word's meaning, easy to use in your own RAG pipeline.
use_when: You need highly precise search over detailed text and have spare disk space.
skip_when: Storage is tight. Plain embeddings plus a reranker is simpler and close in accuracy.
note: ColBERT stores a vector for every word, so indexes get big. Great accuracy, real storage cost.

name: RAG-Anything
short: Multimodal RAG over text, images and LaTeX.
plain: A heavy framework built on LightRAG that parses PDFs, images and formulas with MinerU and builds a knowledge graph you can ask questions over.
use_when: Your answers live in diagrams, tables and images, not just paragraphs.
skip_when: It's your first RAG project. Start with plain text RAG first.
runs_on: Laptop with good RAM, or cloud
note: Not a small building block. It's a full orchestration layer, so expect a learning curve.

name: LangGraph
short: Build agents as a graph of visible steps.
plain: Lets you design an agent as steps and connections, so loops, waiting, memory and approvals are explicit instead of hidden.
use_when: Your agent needs loops, memory, or a human approval step before acting.
skip_when: You're making a single AI call. Plain API code is enough.
note: Harder to learn than no-code builders, but it shows you the agent loop, which is the point.

name: CrewAI
short: Teams of agents with roles like researcher and writer.
plain: A framework for multi-agent teams where each agent has a role and they hand work to each other.
use_when: Your task splits naturally into roles, such as research, write, then review.
skip_when: One agent can do the job. More agents means more cost and more ways to fail.
note: Remember: agents that share the same model and context can repeat the same mistake.

name: Vercel AI SDK
short: One TypeScript API for OpenAI, Claude, Gemini and more.
plain: A JavaScript and TypeScript toolkit for chat apps and agents, with streaming, tool calling and structured JSON output, and one interface across model providers.
use_when: You're building a web app that streams answers or switches between models.
skip_when: It's a small single-model script. Direct API calls are enough.
note: Lightweight and frontend-friendly compared with LangChain.

name: Temporal
short: Makes long-running agents crash-proof.
plain: Records every step your agent takes, so if the server crashes or an API times out, it resumes exactly where it stopped.
use_when: Your agent runs for minutes or days, or waits for a human to approve something.
skip_when: Your agent finishes in a few seconds. The extra setup isn't worth it yet.
runs_on: Your server plus a Temporal server
note: Retries with backoff and human-in-the-loop waits that use no compute while waiting.

name: Promptfoo
short: Automated tests and red-teaming for AI apps.
plain: Runs automatic tests on your prompts, agents and RAG pipelines, including attack tests that try to trick your AI, instead of manual trial and error.
use_when: Before you share an agent with real users, and after every prompt change.
skip_when: You're still on your very first hello-world call.
note: Red-teaming means trying to break your own AI before a real attacker does.

name: LLM Router
short: Sends easy questions to cheap models.
plain: Routes simple queries to cheaper models and hard ones to stronger models, and can learn from your usage over time.
use_when: Your app makes many AI calls and the bill is growing.
skip_when: You're learning and making a handful of calls a day.
note: Savings claims of 30 to 50 percent are the project's own numbers. Test on your own traffic.

name: CodeGraph
short: Maps your whole codebase for AI tools.
plain: Scans every file in your project with Tree-sitter, a fast code parser, so AI assistants understand how your code connects.
use_when: Your project is big enough that the AI keeps losing track of files.
skip_when: Your project is a few files. The AI can read them directly.
note: It avoids slow, unpredictable AI calls by using a real parser.

name: HiveMind
short: Remembers why decisions were made.
plain: Keeps the history behind decisions, discussions and changes, so future agents don't rediscover why something was done.
use_when: You use coding agents across many sessions on the same project.
skip_when: Your project is short-lived.
note: Memory is state, not truth. Check what it stores and who can read it.

name: Graphify
short: Helps AI understand code, images and documents.
plain: Builds a map of your code, images and documents that an AI assistant can use as context.
use_when: Small projects where you want the AI to see how pieces connect.
skip_when: Big projects. It spends tokens, so costs grow with size.
runs_on: Your laptop plus an AI API
note: Good for small projects and history, not for big codebases.

name: Arize Phoenix
short: See every step your agent took, privately.
plain: An open-source tool that shows traces of your agent's steps, tool calls and errors, running locally so your data stays with you.
use_when: Your agent gives a wrong answer and you need to see where it went wrong.
skip_when: You haven't built an agent yet.
note: The privacy-friendly choice for observability.

name: Supabase
short: Database, login and storage in one place.
plain: A hosted Postgres database with login, file storage and row-level security, the rules that decide who can read which rows.
use_when: Your project needs real users, saved data, or login.
skip_when: You're only experimenting in a notebook.
note: I use it in production. Learn row-level security early; it's where most beginner bugs hide.

name: Modal
short: Run Python in the cloud, pay per second.
plain: Write a Python function, and Modal runs it on cloud machines, including GPUs, without you setting up a server.
use_when: Your model or RAG service is too heavy for your laptop.
skip_when: Your code runs fine locally or on a free host.
cost: Pay per use, check free credits
note: I run a RAG service on it. No server to babysit.

name: n8n
short: Drag-and-drop workflows with AI agent steps.
plain: A workflow builder where you connect apps like Gmail, Slack and Supabase with AI steps, without writing a backend.
use_when: You want to automate a real task this week.
skip_when: Your goal is to understand how agents work inside. Code one first.
cost: Free to self-host; paid cloud plans
note: Fair-code, not open source: the code is public under n8n's Sustainable Use License. Connects to 1500+ apps out of the box.

name: Dify
short: Visual builder for AI apps and RAG.
plain: An open-source platform to build chat apps, RAG pipelines and agents with a visual editor.
use_when: You need a working internal tool or MVP fast.
skip_when: You're learning the fundamentals of agents in code.
note: Self-hosting keeps control and avoids per-agent fees.

name: LangSmith
short: Replay and debug failed agent runs.
plain: A dashboard that records your agent's runs so you can replay a failure step by step and fix it.
use_when: You build with LangChain or LangGraph and need to debug.
skip_when: You want everything local and private. Try Arize Phoenix.
cost: Free tier (5k traces a month), then paid
note: Very polished for debugging.

name: Docker
short: Package your app so it runs the same everywhere.
plain: Bundles your code with everything it needs into a container, so the app that works on your laptop works the same way on a server or someone else's machine.
use_when: You're deploying an API or RAG service, or your setup steps keep breaking on other machines.
skip_when: You're only running a notebook or one script. A virtual environment is enough.
cost: Free for personal use; big companies pay
note: On Windows, Docker Desktop usually runs through WSL 2 and needs 8 GB of RAM. Companies with 250+ staff or $10M+ revenue need a paid plan.

name: 21st.dev
short: UI components from a prompt.
plain: Describe the component you need and get ready-made interface pieces for your React app.
use_when: You need a polished UI fast for a project demo.
skip_when: You're learning CSS and layout basics.
note: Great for speed. Still read the code it gives you.

name: Teachable Machine
short: Train an image or sound model, no code.
plain: Google's browser tool where you teach a model to recognise your own images, sounds or poses in minutes.
use_when: You want to feel how machine learning learns from examples.
skip_when: You need a production model.
note: The fastest way to understand training data before any theory.

name: alphaXiv
short: Read and discuss research papers.
plain: A place to read AI research papers with discussion alongside, so hard papers are easier to follow.
use_when: You want to go from blog posts to the original research.
skip_when: You're still learning the basics.

name: Notion MCP
short: Your AI assistant reads and writes Notion.
plain: Connects Notion to your AI assistant so it can search your pages, read notes and draft new pages for you.
use_when: Your notes and plans live in Notion and you want the AI to use them.
skip_when: Your workspace has private pages you don't want an assistant to see. Limit access first.
get_it: Add Notion in your AI app's connectors
note: I use this daily. Decide which pages it can see before you connect.

name: GitHub MCP
short: Your AI assistant works with your repos.
plain: Lets an AI assistant read issues, pull requests and code in your GitHub repositories.
use_when: You want the assistant to review PRs or summarise issues.
skip_when: You haven't set permissions. Start with read-only access.
note: Every new tool is a new attack surface. A malicious issue can carry instructions.

name: Supabase MCP
short: Your AI assistant queries your database.
plain: Lets an AI assistant look at your Supabase tables, run queries and help manage your project.
use_when: You want help writing queries or understanding your schema.
skip_when: It's pointed at production data. Use a development project and read-only mode.
note: Decision is not authority. Don't let an assistant change production data unchecked.

name: Playwright MCP
short: Your AI assistant controls a browser.
plain: Lets an AI assistant open a real browser, click and type, so it can test your web app like a user would.
use_when: You want an assistant to check that your site's main flows still work.
skip_when: Using it on sites you don't own or against their terms.

name: Context7 MCP
short: Up-to-date library docs for your assistant.
plain: Feeds current documentation for libraries into your AI assistant, so it stops suggesting outdated code.
use_when: The assistant keeps using old versions of a library's API.
skip_when: You're using stable, older tools the assistant already knows well.

name: REA
short: Lets your AI agent inspect how existing software works.
plain: Reverse Engineer Anything: an MCP server and command-line tool that inspects apps, websites and binaries on your computer and hands your AI agent the evidence, like components, libraries and code references.
use_when: You want to understand how a feature in an existing app works before building your own version.
skip_when: You already have the source code, or you don't have permission to inspect the software.
runs_on: Your laptop, through your AI app
note: Analysis runs locally, but your agent still sends the results to its model provider. Deep analysis of compiled programs needs Hopper, Ghidra or IDA.

name: LlamaIndex
short: Connect an LLM to your own documents and data.
plain: A framework for RAG apps: it loads your PDFs, notes and databases, splits and indexes them, and finds the right parts for the AI to answer from.
use_when: You want a chatbot or agent that answers from your own notes, docs or company data.
skip_when: Your data fits in one prompt. Just paste it in.
cost: Free, MIT licence; paid cloud parsing is optional
note: Uses OpenAI by default; you can switch to another provider or a free local model.

name: Playwright
short: Code that drives a real browser: click, type, check.
plain: Microsoft's browser automation library. Your script opens Chromium, Firefox or WebKit, clicks, types and reads the page, so you can test a site or automate a browser task.
use_when: You want to test your web app's flows, or repeat the same browser steps every day.
skip_when: The site has an API for what you need, or its terms don't allow automated browsing.
note: Also for Python (pip install playwright). Playwright MCP lets an AI agent use it for you.

name: Gitleaks
short: Finds API keys and passwords hiding in your Git history.
plain: A small, fast scanner that checks your repo, folders and every past commit for leaked secrets like API keys, tokens and passwords. It runs on your laptop with no AI and no account.
use_when: Always. Run it before you push, or add it as a pre-commit hook.
skip_when: Never really. It takes seconds.
runs_on: Your laptop, pre-commit hooks, GitHub Actions
note: Mac: brew install gitleaks. Then run: gitleaks git .

name: Semgrep
short: Rules that catch insecure code patterns, no AI needed.
plain: A fast code scanner for 30+ languages. It matches patterns linked to bugs, like SQL injection or dangerous functions, using community rules or rules you write that look like your own code.
use_when: You want a quick, repeatable check on every commit or in CI.
skip_when: You need bugs that cross many files. The free version looks one file at a time.
note: Then run: semgrep scan --config auto .

name: Cloudflare Security Audit
short: A skill that turns your coding agent into a security team.
plain: Cloudflare's open-source skill for coding agents. One agent maps your app, others hunt for bugs, and a fresh agent tries to disprove each finding, so the report sorts issues into confirmed, needs validation and rejected.
use_when: You build with Claude Code or Codex and want a careful, read-only review of your own repo.
skip_when: Your agent can't run sub-agents, or you need it to run untrusted code without a proper sandbox.
runs_on: Your coding agent, on your laptop
cost: Free, MIT (your agent's model usage is extra)
note: Needs Node.js for its report checks. No Cloudflare account needed.

name: Shannon
short: An AI pentester that proves a bug with a real exploit.
plain: Keygraph's autonomous pentester for web apps and APIs. It reads your source code to find attack paths, then runs real exploits against your app to show which weaknesses are genuine.
use_when: You're about to release and want a deeper test in a safe copy of your app.
skip_when: You can't use an isolated test setup. It really attacks the target, so never point it at production.
cost: Free, AGPL-3.0 (you pay for the LLM)
note: Needs Docker and Node.js 18+. Test only apps you own.

name: Trail of Bits Skills
short: Specialist security skills from a top audit firm.
plain: A marketplace of plugins for Claude Code and Codex from the security firm Trail of Bits: code auditing, static analysis, finding the same bug elsewhere (variant analysis), GitHub Actions checks and smart contract audits.
use_when: You found one bug and want to know if the same mistake hides anywhere else.
skip_when: You're just starting out. Begin with Gitleaks and Semgrep first.
note: Codex: codex plugin marketplace add trailofbits/skills
